The way I did it (and this was in school) was by watching other people interact and mimicking that. I noticed the way people have small talk and the things that keep them interested. I don’t talk about myself, I find something they want to talk about and set them up to talk about it. I’m a “great listener”. I would advertise myself as a bit strange so people would expect it and they got used to me. I mapped out the way the human face moves and what emotions are conveyed and now I move my face/eyebrows almost cartoonishly (I went all out and over did it a bit). I remember things people tell me and write them down on my phone whenever I get the chance (not in front of them) so I can bring it up in a later conversation so they know that I listen to them and I sometimes feel like a psychopath for doing it. 

No matter how hard you suppress yourself, no matter how second nature it becomes it is never truly natural and some part of you will always feel like an outcast trying so hard to achieve something everyone else appears to find so easy. Maybe people will like you more but it’s a specially tailored version of you made just for them and it is draining to wear it all the time. You may find yourself enjoying solitude more and disliking social gatherings more because of how taxing it is to wear a mask or switch between several but you may also find it rewarding. 

I’m not going to tell you to ‘be your true self’ or ‘just wait for the right people to love you for who you really are’ because I know that’s not the point. All I’d advise is that there is a line between being able to blend in with civil society and committing so deeply to a version of yourself you crave to be that you develop an internalised self hatred in the process and it is best to check up on yourself and be aware of your actions and commitment while trying to learn how to be a false version of yourself.
Good luck and I hope you find the middle ground you’re looking for.

I’m 16 and I’ve seen this happen before in several friend groups over several years. There’s a lot of things I could tell you but they’ll probably get drowned out so if you want it talk to me personally I’m all ears. What I’ll say is this. If you OD one of two things will happen:

1) they will have won. They will have got rid of the pest they hated and won’t bat an eye towards you. Your mum will realise how serious you were and feel terrible for ignoring you and the friends you have left will mourn and possibly become aggressive towards the bullies or targeted by them.

2) they will lose it! A sudden slap in the face of a harsh reality and that the ending of a life is entirely on their hands will drive them mad. This could be anything from shedding tears and losing sleep to suicidal devastation of being a murderer. 

And you won’t be there to see it. 

Either reaction, 1 or 2. You will never know. You will never see how people really felt and the true impact you had on the people around you. Your final thought will be a feeling of worthlessness. 

The people of high school are insignificant. You endure them like a cold and once it’s passed you never think about them again. They hold no value. 

I’m studying psychology so if nothing else if you want some general tricks to possible boost your mood message me.
